turns.assessment: The simultaneous outage of many services and loss of numerous lightpaths converges on the shared ROADM at S15. OCH_LOS on multiple S15-facing lightpaths and AMP_INPUT_LOS on separate outgoing S15 lines show a hard optical blocking event at S15, while unchanged measurements on the S19-S10-S21 portion of svc186 exclude that upstream route. A WSS input-port failure at S15 best explains the multi-channel optical loss; an OTN switch failure would not explain OCH or amplifier input LOS.

proposals.rationale: E1 is the sole optical element shared by all affected working paths. The abrupt, simultaneous multi-channel OCH_LOS and loss of input to amplifiers on several S15 egress lines are characteristic of a hard WSS port block at roadm.S15.

A switch-fabric failure at S15 could interrupt many services crossing the node, but it should produce ODU-layer AIS while leaving optical carriers present, contrary to the extensive OCH_LOS and AMP_INPUT_LOS.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A disconnected common optical patch at S15 could cause a hard all-channel loss, but a normal OMS input patch is degree-specific and is less consistent with simultaneous losses across multiple S15 directions.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

clarify.assessment: The evidence localizes the fault to roadm.S15 but does not identify which of the five resolved WSS input ports failed. The simultaneous downstream losses do not uniquely trace back to one ingress port, and the unchanged monitors do not distinguish a WSS port block because they observe optical power before or outside the blocked switching path. A repair at any specific candidate would therefore be speculative.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (5 locations); reported as a set

score.why: truth not in the reported set
